questions.question: 1. Which of the following best describes why large language models (LLMs) outperform n-gram models?
options: LLMs use probabilistic distributions to handle unseen words
LLMs account for contextual relationships over long distances
LLMs reduce vocabulary size for faster processing
LLMs simplify complex tasks by discarding infrequent data
questions.correctAnswer: LLMs account for contextual relationships over long distances
questions.explanation: LLMs use embeddings and transformer architectures to capture long-range dependencies effectively.

questions.question: 2. When evaluating an n-gram model, which of the following issues is not addressed by perplexity?
options: Performance on unseen word sequences
The ability to handle syntactic correctness
Comparison of models on the same dataset
Measurement of model entropy
questions.correctAnswer: The ability to handle syntactic correctness
questions.explanation: Perplexity measures how well a model predicts a test set but does not explicitly assess syntactic correctness.

questions.question: 3. In Add-1 smoothing, what happens to the relative probabilities of frequent versus infrequent word pairs?
options: The gap between their probabilities increases
The gap between their probabilities decreases
All probabilities remain proportional
Add-1 smoothing has no effect on relative probabilities
questions.correctAnswer: The gap between their probabilities decreases
questions.explanation: Add-1 smoothing reduces the gap between high-frequency and low-frequency word pairs by uniformly adding

questions.question: 4. 4. Which of the following methods is used to interpolate probabilities in n-gram models?
options: Multiplying unigram, bigram, and trigram probabilities
Weighted averaging of higher- and lower-order probabilities
Selecting the highest-order n-gram with sufficient data
Normalizing probabilities to sum to 1
questions.correctAnswer: Weighted averaging of higher- and lower-order probabilities
questions.explanation: Interpolation combines probabilities from different n-gram levels using weights to improve robustness.

questions.question: 5. In a Shannon game simulation, why might an LLM outperform a bigram model?
options: It can assign probabilities to unseen word pairs
It generates words based on deep neural embeddings
It uses prior context beyond two words
It reduces entropy in word selection
questions.correctAnswer: It uses prior context beyond two words
questions.explanation: LLMs leverage context from the entire sequence, whereas bigram models only consider the last word.

questions.question: 6. How does the chain rule of probability contribute to language modeling?
options: By approximating probabilities using higher-order n-grams
By computing joint probabilities of sentences
By reducing the complexity of model training
By ensuring independence between word predictions
questions.correctAnswer: By computing joint probabilities of sentences
questions.explanation: The chain rule allows the computation of joint probabilities by breaking them into conditional probabilities.

questions.question: 8. Why might backoff methods outperform higher-order n-gram models in certain contexts?
options: They avoid overfitting by relying on simpler models
They reduce the computational cost of model evaluation
They inherently perform better on sparse datasets
They rely only on unigram probabilities for simplicity
questions.correctAnswer: They avoid overfitting by relying on simpler models
questions.explanation: Backoff methods generalize better when data for higher-order n-grams is sparse.

questions.explanation: Add-1 smoothing adds 1 to the numerator and increases the denominator by the vocabulary size.

questions.question: 11. Which of the following is False?
options: Training a model means finding parameters that predict outputs well from input/output pairs of training dataset
Model is a family of equations
Supervised learning can be applied for mapping from one or more inputs to a single output only
Parameters affect outcome of a equation
questions.correctAnswer: Supervised learning can be applied for mapping from one or more inputs to a single output only
questions.explanation: Supervised learning can be applied for mapping from one or more inputs to one or more outputs

questions.question: 12. Which of the following is an example of supervised learning?
options: Clustering customer data based on p urchase history
Predicting price of mobile based on historical data
Identifying topics in a set of text documents without labels
Discovering associations between products in a shopping cart
questions.correctAnswer: Predicting price of mobile based on historical data
questions.explanation: Mobile price prediction can be solv ed by regression having supervised data available

questions.question: 13. What is the mathematical definition of the ReLU activation function?
options: f(x) = tanh(x)
f(x)=max(0,x)
questions.correctAnswer: f(x)=max(0,x)
questions.explanation: Relu(x) = 0 if x< 0; otherwise x if x>=0

questions.question: 14. In Gradient Descent, what happens if the learning rate is too high?
options: The algorithm converges faster to the global minimum.
The algorithm may overshoot the minimum and fail to converge.
The algorithm will get stuck in a local minimum.
The algorithm will converge to the correct minimum, but it will take longer.
questions.correctAnswer: The algorithm may overshoot the minimum and fail to converge.
questions.explanation: If the learning rate is too high, the updates may overshoot the minimum, causing the algorithm to fail to converge or oscillate around the optimal solution.

questions.question: 15. In backpropagation, why is the chain rule used?
options: To compute the output of the network during forward propagation.
To calculate the gradients of the loss function with respect to weights in each layer.
To determine the optimal number of neurons in a hidden layer.
To update weights by directly minimizing the loss function.
questions.correctAnswer: To calculate the gradients of the loss function with respect to weights in each layer.
questions.explanation: The chain rule i s used in backpropagation to calculate how the loss function changes with respect to each weight by considering the contribution of every layer in the network. This is essential for propagating gradients backward and updating the weights effectively.

questions.question: 16. Consider a simple neural network with: An input layer containing 3 neurons, A hidden layer containing 4 neurons and an output layer containing 2 neurons. The activation functions for the hidden and output layers are ReLU and softmax, respectively. Wha t is the total number of weights (parameters) in this network, excluding biases?
questions.explanation: Weights between input and hidden layer: 3 * 4 = 12 Weights between hidden and output layer: 4 * 2 = 8 Total no of parameters: 12 + 8 = 20.

questions.question: 17. Consider a neural network with a single weight w. The output of the network is given by y = w^2 and the loss function is L = 1/2(y - t)^2 where t=4 is the target value. If the current value of w is 3, what is the gradient of L with respect to w?
questions.explanation: Compute y = w^2 = 3^2 = 9 Gradient of L with respect to y= ∂L/∂y = y - t = 9 - 4 = 5 Gradient of y with respect to w: ∂y/∂w=2w= 2*3 = 6 Using the chain rule: ∂L/∂w=∂L/∂y * ∂y/ ∂w = 5 ⋅6=30

questions.question:
18. In 1D Linear Regression, the least squares loss function is given by:

$$L = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^N (y_i - (\hat{w}x_i + b))^2$$

where y i are the true values, x i are the inputs, w^ is the weight, b is the bias, and N is the number of data points. If x=[1,2,3], y = [2, 4, 6] , w^=2, and b=0, what is the value of the least squares loss?
questions.explanation: Solution: 1. Compute the predicted values : y^i=w^xi+b=2xi+0; For x=[1,2,3], y^=[2,4,6] 2. Calculate the residuals (yi−y^i): Residuals=[2−2,4−4,6−6]=[0,0,0] 3. Compute the least squares loss: L=1/N(yi−y^i)2 = ⅓(0)^2 = 0

questions.question: 19. Which of the following is a key difference between static embeddings (e.g., Word2Vec, GloVe) and contextual embeddings (e.g., BERT, ELMo)?
options: Static embeddings generate different vectors for the same word based on its context, while contextual embeddings generate a single vector per word.
Static embeddings rely on matrix factorization, while contextual embeddings are based on co-occurrence matrices.
Static embeddings assign one vector per word type, while contextual embeddings produce distinct vectors for each token based on context.
Static embeddings cannot capture semantic relationships, while contextual embeddings can.
questions.correctAnswer: Static embeddings assign one vector per word type, while contextual embeddings produce distinct vectors for each token based on context.
questions.explanation: Option (C) is the correct answer according to NPTEL DLNLP Assignment 3.

questions.question: 20. In the context of distributional semantics, why is Pointwise Mutual Information (PMI) often used for weighting co-occurrence matrices?
options: It is computationally efficient for high-dimensional data.
It emphasizes frequent words, which are more important in natural language.
It highlights statistically significant word co-occurrences relative to their independent probabilities.
It directly computes dense vector embeddings from sparse matrices.
questions.correctAnswer: It highlights statistically significant word co-occurrences relative to their independent probabilities.
questions.explanation: Option (C) is the correct answer according to NPTEL DLNLP Assignment 3.

questions.question: 21. What is the primary challenge in using Skip-gram with Negative Sampling (SGNS) to create word embeddings?
options: Optimizing the number of negative samples for each positive sample.
Ensuring that the embeddings are sparse and interpretable.
Balancing the dimensionality of embeddings with training efficiency.
Constraining embeddings to align with matrix factorization methods like SVD.
questions.correctAnswer: Optimizing the number of negative samples for each positive sample.
questions.explanation: Option (A) is the correct answer according to NPTEL DLNLP Assignment 3.

questions.question: 22. If the cosine similarity between the embeddings of "car" and "automobile" is 0.9, while the cosine similarity between "car" and "bike" is 0.5, what can be inferred about the embeddings?
options: "Car" and "automobile" co-occur more frequently than "car" and "bike."
The embedding model has effectively captured semantic similarity between words.
"Car" and "automobile" have identical embeddings.
"Car" is syntactically closer to "bike" than to "automobile."
questions.correctAnswer: The embedding model has effectively captured semantic similarity between words.
questions.explanation: Option (B) is the correct answer according to NPTEL DLNLP Assignment 3.

questions.question: 23. The GloVe objective function minimizes:
options: The binary cross-entropy between predicted and actual co-occurrence probabilities.
The weighted least square difference between the dot product of embeddings and the logarithm of co-occurrence counts.
The negative log-likelihood of the context word given the center word.
The squared error between the word embedding norms and their PMI values.
questions.correctAnswer: The weighted least square difference between the dot product of embeddings and the logarithm of co-occurrence counts.
questions.explanation: Option (B) is the correct answer according to NPTEL DLNLP Assignment 3.

questions.question: 24. Suppose you train a Skip-gram model with Negative Sampling on a vocabulary of 10,000 words. If you choose k=5 negative samples per positive pair, how many updates will be made to the embeddings for each target-context pair?
options: 5 updates (for negative samples only).
1 update (for the positive pair only).
6 updates (1 positive + 5 negative).
2 ⋅ 5=102 \cdot 5 = 102 ⋅ 5=10 updates (one for each embedding matrix).
questions.correctAnswer: 6 updates (1 positive + 5 negative).
questions.explanation: Option (C) is the correct answer according to NPTEL DLNLP Assignment 3.

questions.question: 25. In hierarchical softmax, the computational efficiency is improved by:
options: Reducing the number of parameters using shared embeddings.
Structuring the vocabulary into a binary tree, where calculating P(c ∣ w) depends on the path from the root to c.
Applying negative sampling to approximate the softmax.
Using a fixed-size context window for every target word.
questions.correctAnswer: Structuring the vocabulary into a binary tree, where calculating P(c ∣ w) depends on the path from the root to c.
questions.explanation: Option (B) is the correct answer according to NPTEL DLNLP Assignment 3.

questions.question: 26. FastText improves on Word2Vec by representing words as bags of n-grams. If FastText encounters an out-of-vocabulary (OOV) word, how is the representation of this word constructed, and what are the key limitations of this approach?
options: The vector is constructed by averaging the embeddings of its character n-grams, and the limitation is reduced representation quality for highly uncommon n-grams.
The vector is constructed by summing embeddings of similar words, and the limitation is computational inefficiency.
The vector is learned using hierarchical softmax, and the limitation is the lack of support for hashing-based memory constraints.
The vector is directly inferred using bilingual dictionaries, and the limitation is dependence on cross-lingual data.
questions.correctAnswer: The vector is constructed by averaging the embeddings of its character n-grams, and the limitation is reduced representation quality for highly uncommon n-grams.
questions.explanation: Option (A) is the correct answer according to NPTEL DLNLP Assignment 3.

questions.question: 27. Canonical Correlation Analysis (CCA) is often used to project embeddings into a shared space. Given two languages with highly divergent syntactic structures, which limitation of CCA might reduce its effectiveness, and what alternative approach could address this?
options: CCA assumes linear transformations, making it less effective; using adversarial training for non-linear transformations is a viable alternative.
CCA requires large bilingual dictionaries, making it impractical; autoencoders can bypass this requirement.
CCA is computationally expensive for high-dimensional embeddings; dimensionality reduction via PCA can help.
CCA minimizes mean squared errors, which ignores semantic similarity; graph-based representations offer an alternative.
questions.correctAnswer: CCA assumes linear transformations, making it less effective; using adversarial training for non-linear transformations is a viable alternative.
questions.explanation: Option (A) is the correct answer according to NPTEL DLNLP Assignment 3.

questions.question: 28. Joint optimization methods for cross-lingual embeddings balance monolingual and cross-lingual objectives. For a low-resource language paired with a high-resource language, which factors critically affect the balance, and why?

The quality of the bilingual lexicon as it directly influences monolingual loss optimization.

questions.correctAnswer: The size of the monolingual corpus for the low-resource language as it determines the effectiveness of pretraining.
questions.explanation: Option (A) is the correct answer according to NPTEL DLNLP Assignment 3.

questions.question: 31. Which of the following is the primary cause of the vanishing gradient problem in deep neural networks, particularly in Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs)?
options: The network's weight matrices become too large, causing instability. 2. Gradients become too small during backpropagation, effectively preventing weight updates in the earlier layers.
The activation functions used in the network are too complex and cannot be computed efficiently.
The network suffers from an excessive number of layers, leading to too much redundancy in the model.
questions.correctAnswer: The activation functions used in the network are too complex and cannot be computed efficiently.
questions.explanation: The vanishing gradient problem occurs when gradients become very small during backpropagation, especially in deep or recurrent networks, making it difficult for the model to update the weights in earlier layers. This can slow down or even stop the learning process.

questions.question: 33. In an encoder -decoder architecture for machine translation, the encoder processes an input sequence of length T with a hidden state size of H, and the decoder generates an output sequence of length T′ with a hidden state size of H′. If the encoder’s weight matrix has dimensions H×H for the hidden state transition and V in×H for the input -to-hidden transformation (where V in is the vocabulary size), and the decoder's weight matrix has dimensions H′×H′ for the hidden state transition and V out×H′ for the output -to-hidden transformation (where V out is the target vocabulary size), how many parameters are there in the encoder and decoder combined, excluding biases?
options: V in×H+H×H+V out×H′+H′×H′
V in×H+H×H′+V out×H+H′×H
V in×H+H×H+V out×H′+H′×H′
V in×H+H×H′+V out×H+H′×H
questions.correctAnswer: V in×H+H×H+V out×H′+H′×H′
questions.explanation: ● The encoder's weight matrix for input -to-hidden has V in×H parameters, and for hidden state transitions, there are H×H parameters. ● The decoder's weight matrix for output -to-hidden has V out×H′ parameters, and for hidden state transitions, there are H′×H′ parameters. Thus, the total number of parameters is: Vin×H+H×H+V out×H′+H′×H′

questions.question: 34. In an LSTM network, the number of parameters for the input gate is determined by the size of the input vector V and the size of the hidden state H. Assuming the LSTM has 1 input gate, 1 forget gate, 1 output gate, and 1 cell state, how many parameters are there for the input gate, excluding biases?
options: V×H+H×H
(V+H)×H
V×H+H×1
questions.correctAnswer: (V+H)×H
questions.explanation: For the input gate in an LSTM, the parameters consist of: Weights from the input vector V to the hidden state H, which are represented by a matrix of size V×H Weights from the previous hidden state H to the current hidden state H, represented by a matrix of size H×H Thus, the total number of parameters for the input gate is V×H + H×H = (V + H) ×H

questions.question: 53. In a multi-head attention mechanism with 8 heads and hidden dimension of 512, if we use a batch size of 16 with a sequence length of 64, what is the total number of operations requir ed for the attention computation across all heads (excluding feed-forward layers) ?
questions.explanation: ### Explanation: For a single head in self-attention with: - Batch size (B) = 16 - Sequence length (L) = 64 - Head dimension (d) = 512/8 = 64 (since total dimension 512 is split among 8 heads) The attention computation involves: 1. Query-Key matrix multiplication: (B×L×d) × (B×L×d)ᵀ = B×L×L operations per head 2. Softmax over the attention scores: B×L×L operations per head 3. Attention-V alue multiplication: (B×L×L) × (B×L×d) = B×L×L×d operations per head For exactly 8 heads: - Query-Key multiplication: 8 × 16 × 64 × 64 = 524,288 operations - Softmax: 8 × 16 × 64 × 64 = 524,288 operations - Attention-V alue multiplication: 8 × 16 × 64 × 64 × 64 = 33,554,432 operations Total operations: 524,288 + 524,288 + 33,554,432 = 34,603,008 operations However , if we're focusing purely on the core attention dot product operations (which is common when discussing attention complexity), the answer would be: - 8 heads × 16 batch × 64 sequence × 64 sequence × 64 dimensions = 33,554,432 operations Answer: C) 33,554,432 The dominant cost in attention mechanisms is the attention-value multiplication which scales with O(B×H×L²×d), where H is the number of heads. This is why the attention mechanism becomes computationally expensive for long sequences.

questions.correctAnswer: Use contextualized token embeddings to compare query and document representations at a finer granularity
questions.explanation: Option (C) is the correct answer according to NPTEL DLNLP Assignment 7.

questions.question: 56. If a multilingual QA system is fine- tuned on an English corpus but evaluated on Hindi queries, which fundamental challenge arises?
options: The inability to align embedding spaces across languages
The loss of syntactic information due to translation errors
The increased computational complexity in the retriever module
The failure of word segmentation methods in low -resource languages
questions.correctAnswer: The inability to align embedding spaces across languages
questions.explanation: Option (A) is the correct answer according to NPTEL DLNLP Assignment 7.

questions.question: 57. In dialogue state tracking (DST), a primary reason for switching from rule- based slot filling to machine learning- based approaches is:
options: ML -based methods can generate entirely novel intents beyond predefined slots
Rule -based methods fail to handle multimodal conversations
ML -based methods allow tracking of implicit user preferences and dynamically adjust to ambiguous user inputs
Rule -based approaches are computationally expensive compared to transformer -based DST model s
questions.correctAnswer: ML -based methods allow tracking of implicit user preferences and dynamically adjust to ambiguous user inputs
questions.explanation: Option (C) is the correct answer according to NPTEL DLNLP Assignment 7.

questions.question: 58. Consider an open- domain chatbot trained on large- scale internet data. Which of the following factors poses the most significant challenge to its deployment in high- stakes applications (e.g., healthcare, finance)?
options: The model’s inability to generate grammatically correct responses
The limited size of the training corpus relative to proprietary datasets
The lack of grounding mechanisms to verify factual accuracy and prevent hallucination
The failure to handle multiple- turn dialogues effectively
questions.correctAnswer: The lack of grounding mechanisms to verify factual accuracy and prevent hallucination
questions.explanation: Option (C) is the correct answer according to NPTEL DLNLP Assignment 7.

questions.question: 59. A major limitation of retrieval -based chatbots compared to generative models is that:
options: They require massive amounts of labeled training data to function
They struggle to provide coherent multi -turn interactions
They cannot generate responses beyond the scope of their training corpus
They fail to incorporate user -specific personalization
questions.correctAnswer: They cannot generate responses beyond the scope of their training corpus
questions.explanation: Option (C) is the correct answer according to NPTEL DLNLP Assignment 7.

questions.question: 60. Why do extractive summarization models often fail to perform well in abstractive summarization tasks?
options: Extractive models do not learn semantic relationships between words and phrases
Extractive models depend on lexical similari ty rather than understanding deeper discourse structures
Extractive models cannot handle cross -document coreference resolution
Extractive models lack the computational efficiency required for abstractive summarization
questions.correctAnswer: Extractive models depend on lexical similari ty rather than understanding deeper discourse structures
questions.explanation: Option (B) is the correct answer according to NPTEL DLNLP Assignment 7.

questions.question: 61. In long- document summarization, why might an extract -then- paraphrase approach outperform direct abstractive methods?
options: It preserves factual consistency by constraining s ummaries to extracted content
It eliminates the need for transformer -based architectures
It does not require labeled training data for summarization
It allows for end- to-end training with a lower computational cost
questions.correctAnswer: It preserves factual consistency by constraining s ummaries to extracted content
questions.explanation: Option (A) is the correct answer according to NPTEL DLNLP Assignment 7.

questions.question: 62. While evaluating a summarization model, why is ROUGE -2 sometimes preferred over BLEU?
options: ROUGE -2 correlates better with human judgment for extractive summarization tasks
BLEU cannot handle long documents, whereas ROUGE -2 is designed for multi -document summarization
BLEU only considers single- token matches, while ROUGE -2 evaluates sentence structure
ROUGE -2 incorporates contextual embeddings, making it more robust for summarization
questions.correctAnswer: ROUGE -2 correlates better with human judgment for extractive summarization tasks
questions.explanation: Option (A) is the correct answer according to NPTEL DLNLP Assignment 7.

questions.question: 63. Both dialogue systems and summarization models require sequence generation. Which of the following represents a key distinction between their architectures?
options: Summarization models primarily use extractive methods, whereas dialogue systems rely on seq2seq architectures
Dialogue models generate text interactively based on conversational history, while summarization models optimize for information condensation in a single pass
Summarization models rely on intent classification, while dialogue systems do not
Dialogue models encode sentence embeddings, whereas summarization models use word embeddings
questions.correctAnswer: Dialogue models generate text interactively based on conversational history, while summarization models optimize for information condensation in a single pass
questions.explanation: Option (B) is the correct answer according to NPTEL DLNLP Assignment 7.

questions.question: 64. What is the main advantage of fine -tuning a pretrained model instead of training a model from scratch?
options: Fine -tuning requires a large amount of labeled data to work effectively.
Fine -tuning helps adapt a general model to a specific task while leveraging prior knowledge, reducing data and compute requirements.
Fine -tuning always leads to overfitting and should be avoided.
Fine -tuning removes the need for any labeled data.
questions.correctAnswer: Fine -tuning helps adapt a general model to a specific task while leveraging prior knowledge, reducing data and compute requirements.
questions.explanation: Option (B) is correct based on NPTEL DLNLP Assignment 8.

questions.question: 65. According to the Scaling Laws observed in Super -NaturalInstructions, how does increasing the number of training tasks affect model performance?
options: Increasing tasks improves generalization to unseen tasks, demonstrating positive transfer.
More tasks always lead to overfitting and degrade generalization performance. C) The number of tasks does not impact model performance significantly.
Reducing the number of tasks helps models specialize and generalize better.
questions.correctAnswer: Increasing tasks improves generalization to unseen tasks, demonstrating positive transfer.
questions.explanation: Option (A) is correct based on NPTEL DLNLP Assignment 8.

questions.question: 66. What distinguishes FLAN (Fine -tuned LAnguage Net) models from standard pre -trained language models?
options: FLAN models are instruction -tuned, meaning they are explicitly fine -tuned on a diverse range of tasks formatted as instructions, improving zero- shot and few -shot learning.
FLAN models do not require pretraining and are trained directly on downstream tasks.
FLAN models only work in a zero- shot setting and cannot be fine -tuned further.
FLAN models are based on a completely different architecture than transformer -based models.
questions.correctAnswer: FLAN models are instruction -tuned, meaning they are explicitly fine -tuned on a diverse range of tasks formatted as instructions, improving zero- shot and few -shot learning.
questions.explanation: Option (A) is correct based on NPTEL DLNLP Assignment 8.

questions.question: 67. Which of the following is True about RLHF?
options: RLHF involves state transitions where the agent’s actions influence future states
RLHF does not have state transitions; actions (completions) are scored by a reward model
RLHF attribution of re ward is not done for an entire sequence of actions
RLHF does not use a policy function to determine actions, unlike standard RL.
questions.correctAnswer: RLHF does not have state transitions; actions (completions) are scored by a reward model
questions.explanation: Option (B) is correct based on NPTEL DLNLP Assignment 8.

questions.question: 68. Which of the following is False?
options: Online reinforcement learning allows the agent to continuously adapt to changes in the environment by learning from real -time feedback.
DPO directly optimizes for preference- based feedback, rather than relying on separately developed reward models.
DPO us es computationally expensive sampling process than PPO
DPO simplifies the training framework by eliminating the need to explicitly model rewards.
questions.correctAnswer: DPO us es computationally expensive sampling process than PPO
questions.explanation: Option (C) is correct based on NPTEL DLNLP Assignment 8.

questions.question: 69. In which scenario would DPO be most beneficial?
options: When a clear objective function is readily available for model optimization. B. When aligning a language model with human preferences in a way that avoids explicit reward modeling and complex reinforceme nt learning setups.
For tasks where rapid experimentation and fine -tuning are not necessary.
When dealing with large datasets of labeled human feedback.
questions.correctAnswer: For tasks where rapid experimentation and fine -tuning are not necessary.
questions.explanation: Option (B) is correct based on NPTEL DLNLP Assignment 8.

70. In RLHF the reward function R(s) is often regularized using the KL divergence between the learned policy π_ϕ and the reference policy π_0 to prevent excessive deviation. The modified reward is given by:

$$R'(s) = R(s) - \beta D_{\text{KL}}(\pi_\phi(\cdot \mid s) \parallel \pi_0(\cdot \mid s))$$

The KL divergence is defined as:

$$D_{\text{KL}}(\pi_\phi \parallel \pi_0) = \sum_a \pi_\phi(a \mid s) \log \frac{\pi_\phi(a \mid s)}{\pi_0(a \mid s)}$$

Consider a state s where the action probabilities under $\pi_\phi$ and reference policy $\pi_0$ are:
• $\pi_\phi(a_1 \mid s) = 0.6, \quad \pi_\phi(a_2 \mid s) = 0.4$
• $\pi_0(a_1 \mid s) = 0.5, \quad \pi_0(a_2 \mid s) = 0.5$

72. Which of the following is False?
options: In Few -shot prompt paradigm, for the same prompt the order in which samples are provided can not make the difference in result

Induction head attends back to previous tokens that were followed by the current and/or recent tokens.

questions.correctAnswer: In Few -shot prompt paradigm, for the same prompt the order in which samples are provided can not make the difference in result

questions.question: 73. Which of the following best describes the difference between zero -shot and few -shot prompting in large language models?
options: Zero -shot prompting provides multiple examples in the prompt, whereas few -shot prompting provides no examples.
Zero -shot prompting requires a fine -tuned model, whereas few -shot prompting does not.
Zero -shot prompting relies on the model’s pre -trained knowledge without examples, while few-shot prompting includes a few examples to guide the model.
Few -shot prompting is only applicable to classification tasks, whereas zero -shot prompting works for all NLP tasks.
questions.correctAnswer: Zero -shot prompting relies on the model’s pre -trained knowledge without examples, while few-shot prompting includes a few examples to guide the model.
questions.explanation: Option (C) is the correct answer according to NPTEL DLNLP Assignment 9.

questions.question: 74. A student is solving the following mathematical problem using Chain of Thought (CoT) prompting: Problem: If a bookstore sells 3 books for $15, how much would 7 books cost at the same rate? Using CoT prompting, the model breaks down the problem step by step: The cost of one book is calculated as: 15÷3=5 The cost of 7 books is then determined as: 5×7=35 The final answer is $35. What is the main advantage of using Chain of Thought (CoT) prompting in solving mathematical problems like the one above?
options: It allows the model to generate more creative answers instead of strictly numerical ones.
It enables the model to follow a step -by-step reasoning process, reducing errors in multi -step calculations.
It makes the model answer faster by skipping intermediate steps.
It ensures that the model always provides the correct answer, regardless of input complexity.
questions.correctAnswer: It enables the model to follow a step -by-step reasoning process, reducing errors in multi -step calculations.
questions.explanation: Option (B) is the correct answer according to NPTEL DLNLP Assignment 9.

questions.question: 75. What is the primary advantage of Tree of Thought (ToT) prompting compared to Chain of Thought (CoT) prompting in problem -solving with Large Language Models?
options: ToT allows the model to explore multiple reasoning paths and backtrack if needed, improvi ng complex decision-making.
ToT speeds up response time by reducing the number of tokens generated.
ToT eliminates the need for intermediate reasoning steps, leading to more concise answers.
ToT relies solely on fine-tuning rather than prompting techniques.
questions.correctAnswer: ToT allows the model to explore multiple reasoning paths and backtrack if needed, improvi ng complex decision-making.
questions.explanation: Option (A) is the correct answer according to NPTEL DLNLP Assignment 9.

questions.question: 76. Toolformer is a variant of large language models that enhances reasoning by:
options: Training on a much larger dataset without any external tools.
Dynamically calling external tools like calculators, search engines, or APIs to improve accuracy.
Using only Chain of Thought (CoT) prompting without external assistance.
Eliminating the need for tool usage by relying solely on internal knowledge.
questions.correctAnswer: Dynamically calling external tools like calculators, search engines, or APIs to improve accuracy.
questions.explanation: Option (B) is the correct answer according to NPTEL DLNLP Assignment 9.

questions.question: 77. A student is using a Program of Thought (PoT) prompting to solve the following mathematical problem: Find the sum of all even numbers from 1 to 20. Instead of solving it directly, the model generates and executes a Python program to compute the result: total = 0 for num in range(1, 21): if num % 2 == 0: total += num print(total) What is the key advantage of using Program of Thought (PoT) prompting in mathematical problem -solving?
options: It enables models to follow a strict, predefined step-by- step reasoning structure without requiring execution.
It allows models to generate and execute code, improving accuracy for complex numerical problems.
It eliminates the need for logical rea soning by relying purely on memorized answers.
It reduces computation time by avoiding loops and conditionals in the generated solution.
questions.correctAnswer: It allows models to generate and execute code, improving accuracy for complex numerical problems.
questions.explanation: Option (B) is the correct answer according to NPTEL DLNLP Assignment 9.

questions.question: 78. Which if the following is False?
options: Prompt-Tuning optimize the embeddings of a prompt, instead of words.
In AUTOPROMPT, for automatic token label selection, a logistic classifier is trained to predict the class label using the contextualized embedding of the [MASK] token as input.
Tool-augmented Language Model (TALM) first generates a tool input conditioned on the task input text and invokes a tool’s API by generating a delimiter
In-context learning do well for new tasks by updating gradient of the model parameters
questions.correctAnswer: In-context learning do well for new tasks by updating gradient of the model parameters
questions.explanation: Option (D) is the correct answer according to NPTEL DLNLP Assignment 9.

questions.question: 79. A large language model is given the following in -context examples in the format of (input, output) pair as follows: (1,3) , (2,9), (3,19), (4,33) It is then asked to predict the output for Input = 5. questions.explanation: Option (B) is the correct answer according to NPTEL DLNLP Assignment 9.

questions.question: 80. Suppose you are using AutoPrompt with BERT for text classification with 6 classes. What is the number of learnable parameters to decide the label set for all the classes if BERT uses 1024 as the model dimension and the number of label words per class is 3?
questions.explanation: Given: BERT's hidden size = 1024, Number of classes = 6; Number of label words per class = 3 Step 1: Compute Total Label Words Each class has 3 label words, so the total number of label words across all classes is: 6×3=18 Step 2: Compute Learnable Parameters Each label word has a 1024 -dimensional embedding, so the total number of learnable parameters is: 18×1024=18,432 The number of learnable parameters to decide the label set is 18,432.

questions.question: 81. Which of the following is False?
options: Parameter -efficient fine tuning update a small subset of model parameters
Parameter -efficient fine tuning matches performance of full -tuning in many cases
Prefix -tuning adds a prefix of parameters, and freezes all pretrained parameters.
In parameter -effici ent fine tuning, for L layers in the decoder, there will be L adapters
questions.correctAnswer: In parameter -effici ent fine tuning, for L layers in the decoder, there will be L adapters
questions.explanation: Option (D) is the correct answer according to NPTEL DLNLP Assignment 10.

questions.question: 82. Suppose you want to use LoRA to train the GPT -3 model, which has a model dimensionality of 12288, 48 layers and 48 attention heads, for the tasks of text simplification. You are using LoRA only for the query and key matrices, each with a rank of 16. How many parameters will need to be trained?
questions.explanation: For each layer's query projection: ● Matrix A: 12288 × 16 = 196,608 parameters ● Matrix B: 16 × 12288 = 196,608 parameters ● Total per query projection: 393,216 parameters For each layer's key projection: ● Matrix A: 12288 × 16 = 196,608 parameters ● Matrix B: 16 × 12288 = 196,608 parameters ● Total per key projection: 393,216 parameters Total parameters per layer: 393,216 + 393,216 = 786,432 Total trainable parameters across all 48 layers: 48 × 786,432 = 37,748,736

questions.question: 83. Suppose you want to use Adapters to t rain the GPT -3 model, which has a model dimensionality of 12288, 48 layers and 48 attention heads, for the tasks of text simplification. You are using 4 adapters per layer, each with a down -projection of 4. How many parameters will need to be trained appro ximately?
questions.explanation: For each adapter: ● Down -projection parameters: d × r = 12288 × 4 = 49,152 ● Down -projection bias: r = 4 ● Up-projection parameters: r × d = 4 × 12288 = 49,152 ● Up-projection bias: d = 12288 Total parameters per adapter: 49,152 + 4 + 49,152 + 12288 = 110,596 Since we have 4 adapters per layer and 48 layers: Total trainable parameters = 110,596 × 4 × 48 = 21,234,432

questions.question: 84. In LoRA (Low- Rank Adaptation), what is the key mathematical insight that enables parameter efficiency?
options: Using activation functions with higher gradients
Approximating weight updates through low-rank decomposition
Replacing attention mechanisms with simpler alternatives
Pruning redundant neurons during training
questions.correctAnswer: Approximating weight updates through low-rank decomposition
questions.explanation: Option (B) is the correct answer according to NPTEL DLNLP Assignment 10.

questions.question: 85. The NormalFloat (NF4) format in QLoRA is specifically designed to:
options: Handle normally distributed weights more efficiently
Implement normal vector arithmetic operations
Maintain numerical stability during backpropagation
Reduce power consumption during training
questions.correctAnswer: Handle normally distributed weights more efficiently
questions.explanation: Option (A) is the correct answer according to NPTEL DLNLP Assignment 10.

questions.question: 86. Which of the following correctly describes the memory savings achieved with QLoRA’s Double Quantization technique?
options: Reduces memory usage by storing both model parameters and quantization constants in FP16
Compresses both the forward and backward pass during training
Achieves compression by quantizing both model weights and quantization constants
Uses block -wise quantization for improved convergence
questions.correctAnswer: Achieves compression by quantizing both model weights and quantization constants
questions.explanation: Option (C) is the correct answer according to NPTEL DLNLP Assignment 10.

questions.question: 87. Which of the following is False?
options: In case of pruning, a number of parameters are set to zero, the rest are unchanged
In Quantization, no parameters are changed, upto k bits of precision
Magnitude pruning is a type of unstructured pruning
Magnitude pruning selects weights that are very close to zero
questions.correctAnswer: Magnitude pruning selects weights that are very close to zero
questions.explanation: Option (D) is the correct answer according to NPTEL DLNLP Assignment 10.

questions.question: 88. Which of the following is False?
options: GPU memory required for a model can vary with precision and optimizer
Sequence- level distillation maximize the probability of the output generated by the teacher
DistilBERT use only distillation based loss
In general, infixing slightly underperforms prefix
questions.correctAnswer: DistilBERT use only distillation based loss
questions.explanation: DistilBERT use both supervised and distillation based loss

questions.question: 89. Which of the following is False?
options: According to scaling laws of LLMs, the performance of LLMs mainly determined by model size, dataset size and amount of compute
Larger models are more sample efficient than smaller models
Kaplan laws use dynamic learning rate schedule for the training runs
Performance of LLMs improve most if model size and dataset size are scaled up together
questions.correctAnswer: Kaplan laws use dynamic learning rate schedule for the training runs
questions.explanation: Option (C) is correct based on NPTEL DLNLP Assignment 11.

questions.question: 90. Which of the following is /are True?
options: Mixtral has 8x experts in feed -forward layer
LLaMa2 uses RoPE and SwiGLU
QWen model is trained on multilingual data
GEMINI does not support image inputs
questions.correctAnswer: Mixtral has 8x experts in feed -forward layer / LLaMa2 uses RoPE and SwiGLU / QWen model is trained on multilingual data
questions.explanation: Multiple statements are correct: (A, B, C). Specifically: Mixtral has 8x experts in feed -forward layer / LLaMa2 uses RoPE and SwiGLU / QWen model is trained on multilingual data.

questions.question: 91. Choose the incorrect statement from the below options?
options: sparse attention reduces the computation through the use of sparse operations,
Linear and Reformer models scale linearly with the sequence length
kNN lookup do averaging of tokens at long distances
In the kNN -augmented attention layer, the same queries ar e used for both the local context, and for the external memory.
questions.correctAnswer: kNN lookup do averaging of tokens at long distances
questions.explanation: Option (C) is correct based on NPTEL DLNLP Assignment 11.

questions.question: 92. What is the primary goal of Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG)?
options: To eliminate the need for prompt engineering in generative AI applications.
To reduce the cost of training and deploying foundation models.
To replace foundation models with smaller, more efficient models.
To improve the accuracy and relevance of responses from foundation models.
questions.correctAnswer: To improve the accuracy and relevance of responses from foundation models.
questions.explanation: Option (D) is correct based on NPTEL DLNLP Assignment 11.

questions.question: 93. Which of the following statements about the Swish activation function is correct where Swish function is defined as f(x)=x ⋅σ(βx)
options: Here β can not be a trainable parameter, it should be always constant
When β=1.702, Swish closely approximates the GELU activation function.
As β→∞, Swish behaves like the Sigmoid function.
As β→∞, Swish behaves like the ReLU function.

questions.explanation: Multiple statements are correct: (B, D). Specifically: When β=1.702, Swish closely approximates the GELU activation function. / As β→∞, Swish behaves like the ReLU function..

questions.question: 94. Suppose you are using a Transformer model with 100 million parameters for training. For an input sequence of length 20, approximately how many FLOPs will be required in forward propagation? [2 marks]
options: 100 million
200 million
4000 million
2000 m illion
questions.correctAnswer: 4000 million
questions.explanation: For forward propagation, compute FLOPs ≈ 2 × P × N = 2 × (100 × 10^6) × 20 = 4,000 million (4 billion) FLOPs.

questions.question: 95. As per chinchilla’s scaling laws, to train a compute -optimal model of 8B parameters, how many tokens should you ideally pretrain it on?
options: As large as possible
8 B tokens
1.6 trillion tokens
160 B tokens
questions.correctAnswer: 160 B tokens
questions.explanation: Under Chinchilla scaling laws, tokens = 20 × parameters = 20 × 8B = 160B tokens.

questions.question: 96. Suppose you are using T5 bias with n_b = 128. What will be the last index of the bucket which uses a single offset? After this index, each bucket will be used for multiple offset values.
questions.explanation: Option (A) is correct based on NPTEL DLNLP Assignment 11.

questions.question: 97. Which architectural component appears to store multilingual knowledge according to the research?
options: Self-attention mechanisms exclusively
Feed-forward networks exclusively
Self-attention for reasoning and feed-forward structures for multilingual knowledge
Equal distribution across all components
questions.correctAnswer: Self-attention for reasoning and feed-forward structures for multilingual knowledge
questions.explanation: - The research indicates that LLMs employ "English for reasoning (through self-attention) and leveraging multilingual knowledge (through feed-forward structures)."

questions.question: 98. What fundamental insight about multilingual LLMs is revealed by deactivating language-specific neur ons?
options: Models are inherently monolingual and translation occurs post-processing
Models have redundant neurons that serve no purpose
Deactivating Chinese-specific neurons can cause the model to produce outputs in English
Neurons are universally language-agnostic throughout the model
questions.correctAnswer: Deactivating Chinese-specific neurons can cause the model to produce outputs in English
questions.explanation: Option (C) is correct based on NPTEL DLNLP Assignment 12.

questions.question: 99. Based on the LAPE (language activation probability entropy) score, how are "language-specific neur ons" identified?
options: Neurons with high entropy across all languages
Neurons that show consistent response patterns regardless of language
Neurons with consistently low activation for all languages
Neurons with low entropy , indicating preferential activation for specific languages
questions.correctAnswer: Neurons with low entropy , indicating preferential activation for specific languages
questions.explanation: Option (D) is correct based on NPTEL DLNLP Assignment 12.

questions.question: 100. What happens when language-specific neur ons for a particular language are deactivated compar ed to when random neur ons are deactivated?
options: Performance remains mostly unchanged in both cases
Random neuron deactivation severely impacts performance while language-specific deactivation has minimal impact
Language-specific neuron deactivation dramatically reduces performance in that language, while random deactivation has minimal impact
Both types of deactivation improve performance by reducing noise
questions.correctAnswer: Language-specific neuron deactivation dramatically reduces performance in that language, while random deactivation has minimal impact
questions.explanation: - The results table shows that deactivating language-specific neurons reduces performance to near zero for many languages, while random neuron deactivation has minimal impact on performance.

questions.question: 101. What is the primary differ ence between Gradient Ascent (GA) unlearning and traditional fine-tuning appr oaches for LLMs?
options: GA requires no training data at all
GA reverses the direction of gradient updates to increase loss on undesired data
GA is only applicable to transformer -based architectures
GA is exclusively used for removing copyrighted content
questions.correctAnswer: GA reverses the direction of gradient updates to increase loss on undesired data
questions.explanation: GA reverses the direction of gradient updates to increase loss on undesired data

questions.question: 102. Why is using KL divergence preferr ed over cross-entr opy for maintaining model performance on normal tasks during unlearning?
options: KL diver gence preserves the original model's distribution better
Cross-entropy causes too much emphasis on incorrect outputs
KL diver gence requires fewer computational resources
Cross-entropy creates more bias in the output distribution
questions.correctAnswer: KL diver gence preserves the original model's distribution better
questions.explanation: ) KL divergence preserves the original model's distribution better

questions.question: 103. In the practical application of unlearning to remove copyrighted content (Harry Potter), what metric should be used to evaluate the effectiveness of unlearning?
options: Character -level edit distance between outputs
BLEU similarity score between generated completions and ground truth
Human evaluation of literary style similarity
Token-level perplexity on prompt completions
questions.correctAnswer: BLEU similarity score between generated completions and ground truth
questions.explanation: ) BLEU similarity score between generated completions and ground truth

questions.question: 104. In the context of unlearning harmful responses, why does the Random Mismatch appr oach help preserve normal utility compar ed to simple Gradient Ascent?
options: It introduces noise into the model parameters
It forces the model to generate uncorrelated outputs for problematic inputs
It makes the model completely ignore certain types of inputs
It replaces harmful knowledge with beneficial knowledge
questions.correctAnswer: It forces the model to generate uncorrelated outputs for problematic inputs
questions.explanation: ) It forces the model to generate uncorrelated outputs for problematic inputs

questions.question: 105. What theor etical implication about multilingual models is most strongly supported by the finding that intermediate representations in non-English to non-English translation tasks show English tokens?
options: Multilingual models are actually ensembles of separate monolingual models
English serves as an interlingua or conceptual bridge in multilingual models
The finding is merely an artifact of visualization techniques
Language-specific tokens are randomly distributed throughout processing
questions.correctAnswer: English serves as an interlingua or conceptual bridge in multilingual models
questions.explanation: - The emer gence of English token probabilities during intermediate processing when translating between two non-English languages strongly suggests that English serves as an interlingua or conceptual bridge within these models, likely due to the predominance of English in training data.

questions.question: 106. What crucial insight about multilingual model architectur e is revealed by comparing the distribution of language-specific neur ons between FFN structur es and Attention structur es?
options: Both structures contain equal numbers of language-specific neurons
FFN structures consistently contain more language-specific neurons across all layers
Attention structures are responsible for maintaining linguistic features
Language-specific neurons only appear in the encoder section of transformers
questions.correctAnswer: FFN structures consistently contain more language-specific neurons across all layers
questions.explanation: - "Number of language-specific neurons when processing multilingual queries" demonstrates that FFN (Feed-Forward Network) structures consistently contain more language-specific neurons than attention structures across most layers, suggesting specialized roles in multilingual processing.
